text:
jamal: short postmortem follow-up from the 03/22 throughput/latency spike. we need to close the action items and decide if SLOs change temporarily. agenda: owner assignments, short timelines, dashboard gaps, and whether to adjust p95/p99 SLOs or use routing throttles.

priya: i reviewed the metrics. error-budget burned ~6.2% yesterday (24h window) driven by a p99 jump on large-seq requests to model-x. suspicious pattern: cache churn + a corner GC pause on a subset of hosts. recurring every ~3 weeks.

leo: i can own the host-side GC tuning (INF-5001). plan: update JVM flags, run soak on canary hosts, and monitor GC tail latency. target: small canary by 2026-03-29, full roll by 2026-04-05 if stable.

nina: i'll take the cache eviction/regen task (INF-5002). hypothesis: cold cache regen floods downstream and increases p99. plan: add jittered regen and backoff, validate with loadtest. target EOW for patch + runbook snippet.

infra-bot: ticket INF-5001 created (host GC tuning)  owner: leo  due: 2026-03-29.

infra-bot: ticket INF-5002 created (cache regen backoff)  owner: nina  due: 2026-03-26.

jamal: thanks. two dashboard asks: (a) p95/p99 split by model family + sequence-length buckets, (b) throughput vs p99 heatmap by route. priya can you surface which panels are missing?

priya: current dashboards show p95/p99 but not broken out by seq-length. im missing a route-level heatmap. nina can you help wire the seq-length histogram into Grafana?

nina: yes. i'll add bins [0-128,129-512,513-2048,2049+] and include links to the runbook. draft panel by tomorrow morning.

leo: about SLOs: i prefer not to change SLO numbers unless absolutely necessary. we should try routing-based mitigations first (progressive throttles and route weighting) and a short-lived routing policy that demotes very long seq requests to a lower-cost pool. i'll prototype a fthen config.

jamal: ok, routing prototype looks good as first line. if throttling + GC + cache fixes don't bring error-budget burn under 1% in 7 days, then we'll discuss temporary SLO relaxation with automatic unwind.

priya: to be explicit, proposed SLOs now: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 1.2s for interactive routes; throughput target: 200 req/s sustained for model-x family. any objections?

leo: no objections. add A/B throttle config to tickets.

nina: +1. will add the test plan and runbook links to INF-5002.

jamal: assigning owners: INF-5001 -> leo (host GC), INF-5002 -> nina (cache regen), INF-5003 -> priya (dashboard panels + heatmap), INF-5004 -> leo (routing prototype). set tentative deadlines in the tickets.

infra-bot: ticket INF-5003 created (dashboards)  owner: priya  due: 2026-03-25.

infra-bot: ticket INF-5004 created (routing prototype)  owner: leo  due: 2026-03-24.

priya: can someone add a short note in the postmortem about the recurring 3-week pattern? ops should watch the next window. i'll add an annotation and a derived metric to surface recurrence.

jamal: good call. nina please add a recurring-incident checklist to the runbook (what to check first: cache regen, GC, canary load).

nina: done, i'll attach the checklist to INF-5002 and link it from the dashboard panels.

leo: sample throttle snippet i'll test locally:
```
routing:
  route_weighting:
    long-seq-requests: 0.2
    default: 0.8
  throttles:
    - route: /v1/generate
      max_qps: 5
```

jamal: final ask: 24h objection window on any SLO shifts. if no objections, i'll open a short RFC that outlines the automatic unwind (14d) and the specific SLO delta we might take (-10% on p99 margin). please comment.

priya: no objections.

leo: +1.

nina: ACK.

infra-bot: reminder set for 2026-03-24 09:00:00 "SLO remediations rollup sync".
